title: Prefix State Lookup and Counting
summary: While scanning cumulative state, use earlier prefix values as searchable history so a relationship between two prefixes represents a contiguous range.
recognition_signals: the goal concerns contiguous ranges with an exact target relation
negative values make monotonic window shrinking unreliable
the current cumulative state can determine which earlier cumulative state is needed
core_rules: A range from an earlier boundary to the current boundary is represented by the difference between their prefix states.
Initialize the empty prefix when ranges beginning at index zero must count.
Store frequency for counting, earliest index for longest-length queries, or simple presence for existence queries.
structural_steps: update the running prefix at each item
derive the earlier prefix state required by the target
read the appropriate metadata for that prefix
record the current prefix for future ranges

common_confusions.distinction: Prefix aggregate assumes range boundaries are given. Prefix-state lookup discovers qualifying boundaries by searching previous cumulative states.
Sliding windows need a monotonic repair rule. Prefix-state lookup remains valid with signed values because it uses an exact algebraic relation instead of monotonic shrinking.
